title: A Water Balloon in a Box
colour_map: Used in both films, the figures and the sim. Cell wall (the box) TAN outline, thick. Cell membrane thin BLUE line. Large central vacuole (the water tank) PALE BLUE fill. Water arrows and drops BLUE. Nucleus PURPLE. Mitochondria ORANGE. Chloroplasts GREEN. Endoplasmic reticulum TEAL. Cytoplasm light GREY tint. Light rays YELLOW. Stiffness meter: a vertical bar, empty GREY, filling GOLD. All cells are labelled cartoons marked 'schematic', not to scale.

scenes.visual: Title card 'A Water Balloon in a Box' over a celery stalk that droops, then stands straight. Small text: 'schematic drawings, not to scale'.

scenes.tts: A limp stalk of celery stands in water for a few hours, and it can turn crisp again. You drink water every day and stay just as bendy. What is different about the plant's cells?
scenes.visual: Split screen. Left: a limp celery stalk drooping over the rim of a glass; BLUE water pours in, a clock spins 3 hours, the stalk lifts and stands crisp. Right: a cartoon kid drinks a glass of water and bends over, still bendy; a question mark appears between the two halves.
scenes.narration: A limp stalk of celery stands in water for a few hours, and it can turn crisp again. You drink water every day and stay just as bendy. What is different about the plant's cells?

scenes.tts: Start with one of your own cells. A nucleus holds its instructions. A thin cell membrane wraps the cell and controls what goes in and out.
scenes.visual: Zoom into the kid's arm to one round cell, centre screen. A PURPLE nucleus pops in, label 'nucleus'. A thin BLUE line traces the outline, label 'cell membrane'; tiny dots bounce off it and a few pass through.
scenes.narration: Start with one of your own cells. A nucleus holds its instructions. A thin cell membrane wraps the cell and controls what goes in and out.

scenes.tts: Jelly-like cytoplasm fills the inside. A folded network, the endoplasmic reticulum, makes and moves materials. Mitochondria release energy from sugar. Small sacs called vacuoles store water.
scenes.visual: Each part fades in inside the round cell as it is named, with a label: light GREY tint fills it ('cytoplasm'); TEAL folded ribbons beside the nucleus ('endoplasmic reticulum'); three ORANGE bean shapes ('mitochondria'); two small PALE BLUE circles ('vacuoles'). A bracket around all of them reads 'the shared kit'.
scenes.narration: Jelly-like cytoplasm fills the inside. A folded network, the endoplasmic reticulum, makes and moves materials. Mitochondria release energy from sugar. Small sacs called vacuoles store water.

scenes.tts: A celery cell has this whole kit too. Now we turn your cell into a celery cell, by adding one part at a time.
scenes.visual: A copy of the round cell slides to the right; the original shrinks to a corner labelled 'your cell'. A checklist appears at right: '1 box', '2 food makers', '3 water tank', all unticked.
scenes.narration: A celery cell has this whole kit too. Now we turn your cell into a celery cell, by adding one part at a time.

scenes.tts: First, a stiff cell wall closes around the outside. The membrane stays, just inside it. Think of the wall as a cardboard box.
scenes.visual: A thick TAN rectangle snaps around the round cell; the cell's corners stay rounded inside it, leaving gaps at the box corners. The BLUE membrane line is still visible just inside the TAN wall. Label 'cell wall = the box'. A small cardboard-box icon appears beside the label. Checklist item 1 ticks.
scenes.narration: First, a stiff cell wall closes around the outside. The membrane stays, just inside it. Think of the wall as a cardboard box.

scenes.tts: Second, chloroplasts. In green cells, these food makers capture energy from light to make sugar.
scenes.visual: YELLOW light rays slant in from the top. Six GREEN ovals fade in around the cell's edge; small GOLD dots (sugar) bud off them. Label 'chloroplasts = food makers'. The ORANGE mitochondria stay where they were, not mentioned. Checklist item 2 ticks.
scenes.narration: Second, chloroplasts. In green cells, these food makers capture energy from light to make sugar.

scenes.tts: Third, one large central vacuole. It is a water tank, and in a full-grown cell it fills most of the space.
scenes.visual: A big PALE BLUE sac grows in the centre of the cell, pushing the nucleus and other parts to the edges; it is still well inside the BLUE membrane. Label 'large central vacuole = water tank'. Checklist item 3 ticks.
scenes.narration: Third, one large central vacuole. It is a water tank, and in a full-grown cell it fills most of the space.

scenes.tts: Now let water flow in. The tank swells. It pushes the cytoplasm and the membrane outward, until the membrane presses into the corners of the box.
scenes.visual: BLUE arrows stream into the cell from outside the wall. The PALE BLUE tank inflates; the thin GREY cytoplasm layer and the BLUE membrane are squeezed outward and fill the TAN box's corners. Highlight ring on one corner: the BLUE membrane now lies flat against the TAN wall, with the tank inside it, not touching the wall.
scenes.narration: Now let water flow in. The tank swells. It pushes the cytoplasm and the membrane outward, until the membrane presses into the corners of the box.

scenes.tts: The stiff wall pushes back. It holds the rising pressure in, and the cell turns firm. Picture a water balloon filled tight inside a cardboard box.
scenes.visual: Small TAN arrows point inward from all four walls; BLUE arrows point outward from the membrane; they meet. The stiffness meter beside the cell fills GOLD to the top, label 'firm'. Beside it, a side-by-side model: a BLUE water balloon swelling inside an open cardboard box until it fills the corners, labelled 'model'.
scenes.narration: The stiff wall pushes back. It holds the rising pressure in, and the cell turns firm. Picture a water balloon filled tight inside a cardboard box.

scenes.tts: A celery stalk holds many of these firm cells, side by side. Together they hold the stalk up.
scenes.visual: Zoom out: the one cell becomes a tile in a wall of identical firm boxy cells, each with a full PALE BLUE tank. Keep zooming out to the whole celery stalk standing straight. Label 'many firm cells = firm stalk'.
scenes.narration: A celery stalk holds many of these firm cells, side by side. Together they hold the stalk up.

scenes.tts: Now the stalk sits on the counter all day, and it loses water. What happens to the tank, and then to the stalk?
scenes.visual: The firm stalk lies on a kitchen counter; a sun icon crosses the window and small BLUE drops float away from the stalk. A question card: 'tank? stalk?'.
scenes.narration: Now the stalk sits on the counter all day, and it loses water. What happens to the tank, and then to the stalk?

scenes.visual: Predict pause. Question card 'What happens to the tank, and then to the stalk?' holds; 5-second ring timer at bottom right.

scenes.tts: The tank shrinks, so it pushes less. The box is no longer pushed tight. Each cell goes soft, and the stalk goes limp.
scenes.visual: Back in the cell: BLUE arrows now point out of the cell. The PALE BLUE tank shrinks; the outward BLUE arrows on the membrane fade, the TAN push-back arrows fade. The stiffness meter drains to near empty, label 'soft'. Zoom out: the stalk droops.
scenes.narration: The tank shrinks, so it pushes less. The box is no longer pushed tight. Each cell goes soft, and the stalk goes limp.

scenes.tts: Put the limp stalk back in water. Water moves into the cells, the tanks fill again, and the stalk can turn crisp.
scenes.visual: The drooping stalk drops into a glass of BLUE water. Inset cell: BLUE arrows stream in, the tank swells, the meter climbs to 'firm'. The stalk lifts upright.
scenes.narration: Put the limp stalk back in water. Water moves into the cells, the tanks fill again, and the stalk can turn crisp.

scenes.tts: So why does water not stiffen you? Your cells have the shared kit, but no box. With no stiff wall to push against, water cannot make them firm.
scenes.visual: The small 'your cell' from the corner returns to centre beside the celery cell. Its outline is only the thin BLUE membrane; a TAN box outline flashes over it with a RED cross. BLUE water arrows flow in and out in balance; the cell keeps its size and the stiffness meter stays low, label 'no box'.
scenes.narration: So why does water not stiffen you? Your cells have the shared kit, but no box. With no stiff wall to push against, water cannot make them firm.

scenes.tts: Your body is held up a different way. A skeleton of bones does that job. Your body also controls how much water stays inside you.
scenes.visual: Zoom out from the cell to the cartoon kid; a simple white skeleton glows inside the outline, standing the kid upright. Label 'skeleton holds you up'.
scenes.narration: Your body is held up a different way. A skeleton of bones does that job. Your body also controls how much water stays inside you.

scenes.tts: Same shared kit inside, plus a box, a food maker and a water tank. When the tank is full, it pushes the cell out against the stiff box, and a soft plant stands up.
scenes.visual: Final layout: your round cell on the left, the boxy celery cell on the right. The shared kit glows in both; the TAN wall, GREEN chloroplasts and PALE BLUE tank glow only in the celery cell, each with its model label (box, food maker, water tank). The water balloon in the box sits small under the celery cell.
scenes.narration: Same shared kit inside, plus a box, a food maker and a water tank. When the tank is full, it pushes the cell out against the stiff box, and a soft plant stands up.

scenes.visual: End card with Hex mascot holding a small celery stalk. Line: 'Full tank, stiff box: water pressure holds soft plants up.'
